text:
marta: Heads-up - ran a few nsys traces against the nightly serving image and found a weird warmup pattern for short requests (seqlen <= 32). Cache hit rate is dropping after ~120ms for these fast requests, and we're getting a lot of small GEMM fallbacks. link: https://perfetto.host/run/abcd1234 :eyes:

oz: hmm that's odd. Are these requests hitting the same model shard or being routed across variants?

marta: Single shard + same model version pinned. Routing looks constant. I attached the nsys timeline and a small perfetto slice - you can see repeated calls to `attention_fwd` then a bunch of `gemm_fp16_fallback` spikes.

raj: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to reproduce locally

marta: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=trace_nightly ./run_inference_loadtest.sh --seq 16 --qps 200 --duration 60s`

marta: also captured the dispatcher logs with batching policy debug enabled: ```[batcher] policy=adaptive, target_latency_ms=50, observed_seqlen_distribution={8:0.6,16:0.3,32:0.1}``` but the kernel selection logs show a sudden switch to fallback kernels around iteration 300.

liam: any correlation with KV cache evictions? if prefix cache entries are getting evicted then we would lose KV reuse and see more heavy compute.

marta: checked that. KV cache size steady, but hit latency increases from 0.7ms -> 3.2ms before the fallback spikes. Not full eviction but slower lookups.

perf-bot: Perf regression detected: nightly build 2026-03-15 vs baseline 2026-03-10, p90 latency +18% for seqlen<=32 workloads. Trace attached.

oz: Could be a subtle contention on the cache allocator or a new kernel launch semantics that serialized lookup+dispatch. Are the NVTX ranges indicating stalls on `cudaStreamSynchronize`?

marta: yes, nvtx shows short syncs (~200us) happening right before the KV lookup returns. Timeline snippet: `dispatch -> kv_lookup -> cudaSync -> kernel_select -> launch`. The syncs line up with a fallback decision.

raj: My guess: the adaptive batcher increased batch re-eval frequency and is calling kernel selection on the hot path while KV lookups still in-flight, forcing a conservative fallback path. Any change in batcher code recently?

liam: I pushed a batching tweak last week that reduces the window for sequence coalescing (PR #2184). It was meant to lower tail latency for mixed seqlens. Could be related.

marta: good catch. If the coalescing window shrank we might lose prefix overlap and force fresh KV lookups for each mini-batch, increasing lookup latency and causing selection to prefer generic kernels.

oz: Quick experiments to confirm: 1) revert the coalescing window change or set it to previous value 2) run a focused trace with instrumented KV lookup (include `KV_DEBUG=true`) 3) force batcher to wait for KV lookup completion before kernel select.

marta: already ran 1) locally - when I reverted the window, the fallback spikes vanish and KV hit latency stays low (~0.8ms). I didn't record full nsys trace for that run yet.

raj: can you share the log snippet where kernel selection decides fallback? paste here.

marta: ```[kernel_select] seq_len=16, kv_hit_ratio=0.58, estimated_batch_sz=24, selected_kernel=gemm_fp16_fallback, reason=kv_partial_missing```

liam: that kv_hit_ratio looks low for a steady workload. expected >=0.9 when prefix reuse is working. The reduced coalescing window could explain the drop.

oz: Two follow-ups: A) add a soft barrier so kernel selection waits up to X ms for outstanding KV lookups (configurable), B) add telemetry counter for 'kernel_select_waited_for_kv' so we can measure how often this helps.

marta: +1 on both. I prototyped a 0.5ms wait and reran quick test - p90 improved ~10% and GEMM fallbacks reduced by ~80%. Will run full nsys profile tonight and upload.

perf-bot: upload queued: s3://redwood-perf/trace_1993459999_repro_nsx.tar.gz

raj: if that repros, let's do an internal rollback of the batching change and ship a guarded fix (config flag defaulting to old behavior).

liam: agree. Also we should add a regression test: small-seqlen synthetic workload with simulated KV latency variations to catch this in CI.

marta: adding that to the perf-test harness. I'll open PR with rollback + telemetry + synthetic test.

oz: thanks, team. If the nsys trace shows any kernel launch serialization patterns besides the syncs, call it out. I'm wondering if a new CUDA runtime call got introduced in the allocator path.

marta: will do. tl;dr: root cause looks like batching coalescing window change -> reduced prefix sharing -> more KV waits -> conservative kernel selection -> GEMM fallback spikes. Fix path: rollback batching tweak, add KV-aware kernel selection wait, add telemetry & CI test.

liam: :thumbsup: file the PR and tag @eng-runtime for review.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for perf-runner with image redwood/nightly:1993459999 (ETA ~45m)

marta: thanks, infra-bot. I'll post the final nsys link when available.
